composition.name: Composition
composition.description: Indicates that an element consists of one or more other elements. It is the strongest structural relationship: a part exists only as long as its whole does, and cannot belong to more than one whole at a time. Drawn as a solid line with a filled diamond at the whole (source) end.
composition.example: An "Insurance Policy" business object is composed of a "Policy Schedule" and a set of "Policy Conditions" — remove the policy, and its schedule and conditions cease to exist as parts of anything.

aggregation.name: Aggregation
aggregation.description: Indicates that an element combines one or more other elements that are not exclusively its parts — a weaker form of composition where the parts can exist independently or be shared across wholes. Drawn as a solid line with a hollow (unfilled) diamond at the whole (source) end.
aggregation.example: A "Claims Department" business function aggregates the "Claims Intake" and "Claims Assessment" sub-functions, though each sub-function could in principle also serve another department.

assignment.name: Assignment
assignment.description: Indicates the allocation of responsibility, or the assignment of an active structure element to perform behavior, or an active element to a role. Drawn as a solid line with a filled circle at the source (assigned) end and a filled arrowhead at the target end.
assignment.example: The "Claims Handler" business role is assigned to the "Assess Claim" business process, meaning whoever holds that role carries out the process.

realization.name: Realization
realization.description: Indicates that an entity plays a critical role in the creation, achievement, sustenance, or operation of a more abstract entity — typically that a concrete element realizes a more abstract one, such as a component realizing a service, or a requirement realizing a principle. Drawn as a dotted line with a hollow triangle arrowhead pointing to the realized element.
realization.example: The "Claims Intake Component" application component realizes the "File a Claim" application service exposed to policyholders.

serving.name: Serving
serving.description: Indicates that an element provides its functionality to another element — it makes something available for the other element's use. Drawn as a solid line with an open arrowhead pointing to the served element. Renamed from "used by" in earlier ArchiMate versions.
serving.example: The "Payment Processing" application service serves the "Handle Insurance Claim" business process, which relies on it to issue payouts.

access.name: Access
access.description: Indicates that a behavior element or active structure element accesses, reads, writes, or updates a passive structure element such as a business object or data object. Drawn as a dotted line, optionally with a small open arrowhead indicating the direction of access.
access.example: The "Assess Claim" business process accesses the "Claim File" business object to read its contents and update its status.

influence.name: Influence
influence.description: Indicates that an element affects the implementation or achievement of a motivation element, such as a goal or requirement, positively or negatively. Drawn as a dashed line with an open arrowhead, optionally labeled with a + or − sign to show the direction of influence.
influence.example: The "Rising Claim Fraud" driver negatively influences the "Reduce Claim Payout Time" goal, since additional fraud checks slow down processing.

association.name: Association
association.description: Indicates an unspecified relationship, or one not covered by any of the other relationship types, between two elements. Drawn as a solid line with no arrowhead, optionally with an open arrowhead to show a direction of reading.
association.example: The "Policyholder" business actor is associated with the "Insurance Policy" business object — a general link that doesn't imply structural or dependency semantics.

triggering.name: Triggering
triggering.description: Indicates a temporal or causal relationship between behavior elements — that one process, function, or event starts another. Drawn as a solid line with a filled arrowhead pointing to the triggered element.
triggering.example: The "Claim Submitted" business event triggers the "Assess Claim" business process.

flow.name: Flow
flow.description: Indicates the transfer of information, money, goods, or other value from one behavior element to another. Drawn as a dashed line with a filled arrowhead pointing to the receiving element.
flow.example: The "Assess Claim" process flows a "Payout Decision" to the "Process Payment" process.

specialization.name: Specialization
specialization.description: Indicates that an element is a more specific kind of a more general element, inheriting the general element's characteristics while potentially adding or refining its own — directly analogous to generalization/inheritance in object-oriented modeling. Drawn as a solid line with a hollow triangle arrowhead pointing to the general element.
specialization.example: "Auto Insurance Policy" and "Travel Insurance Policy" are both specializations of the general "Insurance Policy" business object, each adding their own specific attributes and conditions.

and-junction.name: AND Junction
and-junction.description: A junction used to connect multiple relationships of the same type into a single logical AND: all incoming relationships must hold together for the outgoing relationship to apply. Drawn as a small filled circle where the lines meet.
and-junction.example: Both the "Payment Received" and "Goods Dispatched" events must occur before the AND-junction triggers the "Close Order" process.

or-junction.name: OR Junction
or-junction.description: A junction used to connect multiple relationships of the same type into a single logical OR: any one of the incoming relationships is sufficient for the outgoing relationship to apply. Drawn as a small hollow circle where the lines meet.
or-junction.example: Either a "Manager Approval" or an "Auto-Approval" outcome is enough for the OR-junction to trigger the "Release Funds" process.
